correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite graphs, a same-part pair has distance two and its shortest paths contain every vertex outside that part, while a cross-part pair is adjacent. Hence one interval step from a set containing two vertices in part \(V_i\) adds all vertices outside \(V_i\). If another part is non-singleton, the new set contains two vertices there and a second interval step fills the remaining vertices of \(V_i\). With exactly one non-singleton part, closure can fill outside it but cannot refill an omitted vertex inside it; with all singleton parts the graph is complete. This proves all three cases and the enumerator. A fresh independent brute closure on every complete-multipartite profile through order six matched the theorem.

Its proof therefore immediately yields the assigned hull theorem by one further closure iteration: a heavy part creates every outside vertex, which creates a heavy second non-singleton part exactly when one exists, and that second pair fills the original part. The one-non-singleton and complete-graph boundary cases are equally immediate. The assigned three-case hull classification, minimal generators, and polynomial are consequently routine corollaries of already published same-object structure, even though 'geodetic set' and 'hull set' are distinct notions.
